criteria.criterion: States the data-loss risk of bootstrapping the wrong node as must-not-do or stop condition
criteria.evidence: "Bootstrapping a node that is behind makes its state the truth, and transactions only the more advanced node held are lost." The Do NOT list includes "Bootstrap a node because it came up first ... Compare positions." Point of no return is also stated.

criteria.evidence: Section A, "Is this really a full outage?": "Any node Primary | Stop. This is a rejoin, not this runbook." The Scope section also excludes a single node down.

summary: This is a strong runbook draft. It meets every expected reasoning point: it identifies the most advanced node using grastate.dat, safe_to_bootstrap and --wsrep-recover. It states the data-loss risk as a must-not-do and gives a decision point for full outage versus partial failure. It also includes end-to-end capability verification, marks unknown specifics as TODOs, and plans a validation run before Friday by a non-author with the expert watching. It commits none of the critical errors. Environment-specific paths and commands are labelled as examples, and there are no book citations.
